svg.title: The server's answer to initialize arriving in three pieces, 10 and 30 bytes and the rest: what kilo's buffer holds after each read(), and the message taken off its front once it is whole
svg.text: the scripted server writes its 171-byte answer to kilo at 07.02 in pieces of 10, 30 and 131 bytes, 0.255 s apart

g.title: read() returns 10 bytes: the buffer holds 10, "Content-Le". No \r\n yet, so not even the header is whole: lspFrame() says 0, wait for more.
g.text: lspFrame() returns 0: no line end yet, wait for more

g.title: 0.203 s later read() returns 30 more: 40 held. The header is whole, Content-Length 148, but only 17 bytes of the body have come: 0, wait.
g.text: lspFrame() returns 0: the header says 148 bytes of body; 17 are here

g.title: 0.306 s later read() returns the other 131: 171 held, the whole message. lspFrame() returns 171: a 23-byte header and a 148-byte body.
g.text: lspFrame() returns 171: a whole message, a 23-byte header and a 148-byte body

g.title: The message is taken off the front: 0 bytes are left, and the buffer starts where the next message will. lspHandle() gets the body, and 07.02 says how long it was.
g.text: taken off the front: 171 bytes; lspHandle(body, 148)
